statement: In MSTR, a push above the prior-day high that prints without perp volume is not accepted: it is sold back under the level within minutes and the move reverses toward VWAP or further, so buyers of the break are the trapped side.

note: 149.72 on no volume, sold back, -300bp after
second rejection at 149.9 rotated to VWAP

statement: When a mega-cap gaps below the prior low and fully fills the gap back above the prior close in the first hour, gap shorts keep covering and the prior close holds as support for the rest of the morning; bought far above VWAP late in the move (after 11:00, >100bp over VWAP) the same read fails.

note: MSFT held prior close all morning, +0.49R
TSLA bought 115bp over VWAP at 11:16, lost prior close

statement: WTI after an overnight gap above the prior high: the first opening leg tops within 15-30 minutes and crude balances around VWAP for one to two hours on heavy two-sided volume before a second leg in the gap direction; chasing the first leg's high chops out and fading the balance high gets run over.

note: bought 102.46 near the first-leg top, chopped and cut
fade of the range high would have been run over at 11:37
range break at 11:43 held the old high

Direct test and it failed: I shorted MSTR at 142.10 precisely because the push above the opening range was printing with sparse volume and zero aggressor trades. It was not sold back under the level, it carried another 180bp to 144.71 and the trade lost 0.40R.

statement: On a session that prints efficiency above 0.8 with no VWAP cross, a limit entry resting at a level price has already left (the VWAP it ran from, a swept prior level) does not get filled: the sidelined buyers lift the offer before price returns, so the retest never trades. In that tape the choice is to pay the spread into the move or rest the order inside the current 15-minute range, not at the price you would have liked.

note: TSLA limit at 389.60 never filled while the trend ran from 389 to 396.9
WTI retest short at 101.33 never filled while crude fell 101.11 to 100.31
NVDA limit at 216.40 never filled while NVDA went to 217.90

statement: Distance from VWAP is not a fade signal on a day when every seller is being absorbed. When a symbol is more than 150bp above VWAP but each new high is met by buyers as aggressors and the pullbacks stop short of the prior swing, the stretched price is acceptance, not exhaustion, and shorting it loses even when the extension prints on sparse volume.

note: MSTR 154bp over VWAP on sparse volume went 250bp further, cost 0.40R
HOOD balance under a falling VWAP resolved up through it instead
refused the same MSTR fade 200bp higher and it held its highs rather than reverting

statement: In MSTR a sweep of a session extreme that prints with no perp volume at all means the forced sellers are already gone, so it marks the turn rather than a trap: the reclaim that follows runs far further than the 15-minute range suggests. Standing aside because nobody looks trapped is the wrong inference from zero volume at an extreme.

note: Stood aside on the zero-volume sweep of 137.49 and MSTR rallied 520bp to 144.71 over the next two hours.

statement: When a mega-cap (NVDA, MSFT) gaps above the prior high on a sparse perp tape, fails, and fully fills the gap below the prior close in the first 45 minutes, the fill marks the low rather than starting a trend down: sidelined buyers take it back to VWAP and the open within the hour. Shorting the fill at its extreme (90bp+ under the open) sells to them; the trapped side is the late gap-fill shorts.

note: NVDA short at 216.12 (-99bp from open) reclaimed VWAP in 14 minutes and reached 218 by 11:45
MSFT failed-breakout short only got a 50bp dip to 528.6, then round-tripped to new highs by 11:10

statement: In TSLA, a gap above the prior high whose first-minute flush below the prior high is bought straight back holds the gap for the whole morning. A later pullback to VWAP during a broad rotation is a pause, not a failure: manage it on structure (back under the prior high or the flush low), not on a VWAP touch or a regime label change.

note: exited +0.14R on the 10:25 VWAP dip; TSLA then ran from 401.5 to 407.6
re-entry on the 11:30 breakout made a new high at 407.64 as the read said

statement: When WTI breaks a whole-dollar round number in a trend down, buyers at the round number push it back above by 30-40bp at least once before the next leg; a stop tightened to just above that retest gets taken minutes before the move resumes. Keep the stop above the prior structural level (the broken prior low), not just above the round number.

note: stop tightened to 100.28 was hit at 100.32 at 11:55; WTI was back at 99.87 by 11:59, the original 100.42 stop held

statement: In HOOD after a large gap down on a name already sold hard (-10%+ over the week), the forced covering happens in the opening burst (first 5-10 minutes, >90% aggressive buying, 10x+ relative volume). After that, later pushes above the morning high print with no perp volume, are sold back under it within minutes and rotate to VWAP: the remaining shorts are not trapped, so buying those breaks for a gap-fill target loses.

note: Three no-volume pokes above 92.16 sold back; closed +0.09R
No-volume break to 92.49 back under 92.16 in 7 minutes, down to VWAP; -0.49R

statement: In TSLA, a gap above the prior high whose first-minutes flush below the prior high is NOT bought back within about five minutes becomes a trend down for the morning: trapped gap longs sell every bounce and price stays under VWAP for 90+ minutes (here -300bp, efficiency above 0.95). Enter at market; limits at or near the bid do not fill in that tape.

note: Short 405.45, trend to 397.4 with no VWAP cross until 11:05; +1.13R
Limit near the bid in the same tape never filled

statement: A morning trend down that has not crossed VWAP for 90 minutes is over once session efficiency falls below about 0.75 and the 15-minute range compresses to a third of its peak: the first VWAP test is then reclaimed and held, not sold. Selling that first retest is selling to the shorts who are covering.

note: TSLA reclaimed VWAP at 11:05 (efficiency 0.7, range 30bp vs 120bp earlier) and held above it to the close
